title: Escalation Budgeting Playbook and Acceptance Clauses for Strategic Customer Roadmap Intake
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Define an operational "escalation budget" and an associated playbook + acceptance clauses to standardize how we evaluate, accept, and commit to roadmap asks from strategic customers. This covers upfront intake governance, maximum committed engineering effort per account (budgeting), SLA tiers for response/commitment, and automated routing + fallback behaviors when budget or capacity is constrained.

Why now: Sales and CSMs report inconsistent expectations across accounts — some requests turn into long blind commitments while others are triaged out with limited visibility. We need a durable mechanism that: 1) gives top accounts predictable decision timelines, 2) limits unscoped engineering drift, and 3) ties acceptance to measurable OKRs and release lanes.

Scope:
- Define escalation budget units (e.g., story points or reserved sprint-days) by customer tier and fiscal quarter.
- Create acceptance clauses that specify minimum information and success criteria for an ask to be considered for the budgeted runway.
- Build a do/deny workflow: intake -> technical review -> product evaluation -> decision + commitment window.
- Integrate routing rules in Linear + Console intake form so requests auto-populate required metadata.
- Define fallback paths (deferred roadmap lane, paid engagement, dedicated capacity request) with templated stakeholder comms.
- Instrument metrics (time-to-decision, % of asks accepted, engineering hours consumed vs budget, regret/rollbacks).

Out of scope for MVP: full billing automation for paid engagements, contractual amendments; these will be follow-up projects.

Deliverables:
- Escalation Budget matrix (by account tier / quarter).
- Acceptance Clause template (PRD checklist + success metrics).
- Linear intake template and automation rules.
- Playbook doc for CSMs + Sales + Eng with decision flows and comms templates.
- Dashboard: budget consumption and pending asks.

Success metrics (tied to OKR):
- Reduce un-scoped roadmap churn by 30% in Q2.
- 95% of top-account escalations receive a decision within 14 business days.
- < 10% of accepted asks require major rework or rollback in the quarter.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Risk: Perceived decreased flexibility by strategic accounts. Mitigation: explicit paid-engagement fast lane and clear SLA tiers.
- Trade-off: Tight budgets may shift work into paid professional services; requires sales alignment and clear comms.

Next steps (MVP):
1) Align stakeholders and finalize budget units (by 2026-02-22).
2) Ship Linear intake template + automation (by 2026-03-08).
3) Publish playbook doc and train CS/Sales (by 2026-03-22).
4) Pilot with 5 strategic accounts in Q2.

Decision points that require input:
- Units: points vs reserved days (engineering prefers days for predictability; sales prefers points for flexibility).
- SLA windows: 7 vs 14 business days for decision time.
- Acceptance criteria strictness for MVP (minimum: impact statement + business metric + owner + expected release window).
